title: {Syn} Paxos Is Small, Subtle, and Everywhere
content:
Paxos is a family of consensus protocols for reaching agreement in an asynchronous distributed system with failures. The basic idea is compact, but the edge cases are famously subtle.

Many production systems use Paxos-like or Raft-like protocols because replicated state needs principled agreement, not just hopeful retries.

Why it matters: algorithms keeps producing ideas that are simple enough to state and strong enough to build with.
